header: THE SEARCH BAR AND THE EMPLOYEE MANAGER (step 66a). When a sentence means "change employee data" (intent.ts), the omnibar either
- opens the manager (a panel in the answer area) for the HOD of C&IT and for an executive he has authorised,
- or says plainly why not: nobody is logged in; the person has no authority; a delegate asked to authorise somebody (only the HOD does that).
The decision uses the LOGIN's ticket (the omnibar's userKey), never anything typed. I read the sentence first (pure); I ask the database only when it IS such a sentence.

members.name: nameOf
doc: I send the logged-in person's name with the answer (optional: without it the panel asks for the name itself).

behaviours: the HOD asks to add an employee: the panel opens (op add, role hod), and nothing else is in the payload
'change dob of goutam debnath': the panel opens to change, with the name as the search
a delegate asks to edit: the panel opens with role delegate and the ticket
a delegate asks to DELETE: one plain sentence, no panel
a delegate asks to authorise or withdraw: one plain sentence, no panel
the HOD asks to delegate: the panel opens on delegation
somebody with no authority: 'Not allowed', no panel
nobody logged in: 'Please log in', no panel
a failing authority check means 'Not allowed' (never open the manager on doubt)
"${q}" is not a change request: null, and the authority was NOT asked
...the database was never asked for any of them
the person is the LOGIN's ticket: a ticket in the sentence is only a prefill, never who is asking
runOmnibar: the HOD's request opens the panel (source tag, attempt 1) before the date lookup, the PAX route, the hospital route and the model
a RETRY (a 'No' on an earlier answer) never runs this route again
a failing route never breaks the omnibar
an older caller without the dependency still works
a question about a date of birth goes on to the date lookup as before
omnibar.ts wires the manager to the application's own connection (getDb) and to the employee manager's authority check
...never to the model's client or its read-only role
...the route comes BEFORE the date lookup, inside the block that a retry skips
the HOD's name is in the payload that opens the manager (so the header has it at once, with no request)
an authorised executive's own name is sent, trimmed
a blank name is left out of the payload (the panel will ask for it)
if the name cannot be read the panel STILL opens, without a name
without a name function (as before) the payload is what it always was
a person who is refused gets no panel, so his name is not sent anywhere
a person with no authority at all gets a plain sentence and no name
a sentence that is not such a request never reaches the name lookup either
the authority and the name are asked TOGETHER (both start before either answers): the name adds no waiting
the search bar's wiring hands the manager the directory's name function (the one the session's actor already uses)
